name: Socialist Conservatism
summary: Combines left-wing economics (public ownership of key industries, redistribution, strong unions, protection of domestic industry) with social and cultural conservatism (family, nation, faith, limits on immigration). Adherents see liberal progressive politics and global markets as joint threats to working-class community, work and solidarity, and are typically Eurosceptic and sceptical of military alliances.
scope: The Western left-conservative mainstream: Orwell's patriotic English socialism in The Lion and the Unicorn (1941), Blue Labour in Britain (Maurice Glasman) and Sahra Wagenknecht's Alliance in Germany. It leans on Wikipedia's account of left-conservatism for the wider family. It excludes Marxist-Leninist state variants, the Chinese party's left-conservatives and South African or Tanzanian ruling-party versions, which differ on one-party rule, religion and monarchy.

keyFigures.name: George Orwell
keyFigures.role: Author of The Lion and the Unicorn, arguing socialism must build on English patriotism and common decency.

keyFigures.name: Maurice Glasman
keyFigures.role: Founder of Blue Labour, which he described as a deeply conservative socialism of family, faith and work.

keyFigures.name: Sahra Wagenknecht
keyFigures.role: Founder of the Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason, described as left-conservative.

sources.title: The Lion and the Unicorn: Socialism and the English Genius (in Fifty Orwell Essays)
sources.author: George Orwell
sources.usedFor: Patriotism, common ownership with private personal possessions, ending hereditary privilege, democracy against totalitarianism, criticism of the left intelligentsia.

sources.title: Left-conservatism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition and core positions on family, abortion, drugs, sex work, immigration, capital punishment and anti-Westernism.

sources.title: Blue Labour
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Family, faith, work, localism, immigration, EU, protectionism, patriotism and corporatist labour relations.

sources.title: Labour isn't working (Maurice Glasman interview)
sources.author: Progress
sources.usedFor: Glasman on immigration and wages, German-model works councils, desert-based fairness, faith and patriotism.

sources.title: Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Programme: nationalisation, taxes on wealth, collective bargaining, immigration limits, deglobalisation, nuclear power, NATO and Ukraine.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Left-conservatism keeps pro-redistribution Marxian or Keynesian economics, and Blue Labour wants services publicly guaranteed but run locally rather than from the centre.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Pro-worker redistribution is the economic core of the tendency; BSW pairs it with stronger collective bargaining, so a substantial wage floor fits.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sources describe left-conservatives as anti-capitalist and sceptical of markets; Blue Labour rejects faith in global markets and BSW wants to limit the market.

public-ownership.rationale: Orwell's programme nationalises land, mines, railways, banks and major industry, and BSW proposes nationalising key industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: BSW seeks higher taxes on the wealthy and redistribution, and Orwell wanted privileged incomes sharply reduced.

unions-good.rationale: Blue Labour says movements must be pro-worker and pro-trade union, and BSW wants collective bargaining strengthened, though Glasman criticised public-sector union power.

property-fundamental.rationale: Socialist economics subordinates private ownership of productive property to common ownership; Orwell keeps only personal possessions private.

regulate-corporations.rationale: BSW calls for state intervention against dominant companies and a limit on the market.

cut-welfare.rationale: They oppose cuts to protection but want welfare tied to work and desert and run locally, so they reject the premise that welfare simply breeds dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Glasman's guild-socialist, German-model works councils and shared burdens point to worker participation, but Orwell and BSW stress state rather than worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Left-authoritarian tendencies and order-minded social conservatism lean toward accepting security measures, but no source states a position on surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to drug legalisation among left-conservatism's core social positions.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Left-conservatives reject New Left identity politics, which makes them unlikely to back speech codes, but sources are silent on hate-speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Orwell's English socialism was explicitly democratic and contrasted with totalitarian Soviet rule; Blue Labour grounds politics in community bodies, not a bypassing leader.

state-harmful.rationale: A tendency built on nationalisation, a strong welfare state and state intervention regards the state as necessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Order-minded left-conservatives probably accept gun control, but no source states a position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Social conservatism and opposition to abolishing capital punishment suggest support for order, though no source gives this directly.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to sex work among left-conservatism's social positions.

decide-locally.rationale: Blue Labour favours local, democratic management of services over a centralised state, and Glasman builds on community organising.

rehabilitation.rationale: Retaining capital punishment and defending order suggest a tougher stance on punishment, but no source discusses prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Family is a central pillar of Blue Labour ("family, faith and flag") and left-conservatism defends the family and traditional values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Left-conservatism is characterised by opposition to LGBT rights, though Western adherents often downplay the issue.

abortion-legal.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to abortion rights as a defining social position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Blue Labour treats faith as part of working-class community life and draws on Catholic social teaching.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: They reject social justice campaigns not tied to class struggle and oppose intersectionality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Left-conservatives are linked to gender-critical feminism, and BSW opposes gender-inclusive language and easier legal gender change.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Blue Labour seeks national renewal and rejects anti-patriotism, and Orwell argues English socialism must grow from English national character.

gradual-change.rationale: Blue Labour calls itself deeply conservative and wants the state to grow out of existing community life, though Orwell wanted a rapid transformation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Blue Labour backs much lower immigration, BSW wants further restrictions to protect the welfare state, and opposition to immigration is a defining trait.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Left-conservatives are Eurosceptic and anti-Western and see supranational bodies as limiting democracy.

free-trade.rationale: Blue Labour supports protectionism and reindustrialisation and BSW advocates deglobalisation and protecting domestic industry.

nation-first.rationale: Blue Labour argues Brexit restores national economic sovereignty against global capital, and BSW favours greater national sovereignty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: BSW criticises NATO and arms deliveries, and left-conservatives are anti-imperialist and anti-Western.

open-borders.rationale: Blue Labour opposes free movement of labour and BSW wants tighter limits on immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose environmentalism and BSW is sceptical of costly green policy and wants industry protected.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: BSW criticises the heating law and combustion-engine ban as costly and ineffective, and left-conservatives oppose environmentalism.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Orwell trusted neither technocrats nor a progress narrative and sources offer no explicit stance, so this is a near-neutral guess.

expand-nuclear.rationale: BSW favours investing in nuclear power and tolerating traditional fuels for a time.

revolution-justified.rationale: Orwell called for a quiet, English-style revolution within the democratic tradition, and Blue Labour is conservative of institutions, so violent revolution is not endorsed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Glasman rejects managerial Fabianism and bossy progressivism, and BSW attacks out-of-touch elites.

central-planning.rationale: Blue Labour follows Polanyi and the German model of regulated markets and local bodies rather than full central planning, though Orwell wanted state ownership.

socialized-markets.rationale: Glasman's German model of works councils and regional banks suggests markets tempered by mutual ownership, but no source states this directly.

land-value-tax.rationale: Orwell wanted land nationalised rather than taxed, and no source supports replacing other taxes with a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Orwell stressed ending inherited incomes and hereditary privilege as a priority of English socialism.

basic-income.rationale: Blue Labour makes the work ethic central and ties fairness to having worked and paid in, which is at odds with unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Blue Labour supports protectionism and BSW wants domestic industry shielded from global markets.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Blue Labour wants reindustrialisation and BSW wants state intervention in the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Orwell keeps personal possessions private and values a home of one's own but puts the means of production under the state, while Blue Labour favours community bodies over both.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in these sources suggests abolishing wages; the tendency keeps wages, collective bargaining and the work ethic.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Orwell would nationalise banks, which implies a public central bank rather than abolition and no market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Blue Labour favours corporatist labour relations and German-style shared decisions between workers and management.

one-party-rule.rationale: Orwell set English socialism against Soviet totalitarianism and called for political democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Orwell thought the royal family could remain as a symbol and Glasman praised pre-war Labour's constitutional conservatism, but Glasman also disliked monarchist ruling-class England.

democracy-best.rationale: Orwell's programme includes political democracy, and Blue Labour wants democratic local bodies, though anti-elite populism complicates support for any voters' choice.

direct-votes.rationale: BSW and populism lean toward popular voice, but Blue Labour prefers community institutions, and the sources give no position on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Glasman likes works councils inside firms, not as the basis of national political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: National renewal and national unity emphases make regional secession unlikely to be supported.

natural-rulers.rationale: Orwell attacked a hereditary ruling class and demanded promotion by ability, not birth.

political-violence-never.rationale: Orwell favoured change without bloodshed and Blue Labour is institution-minded, though no source states an absolute rule.

war-builds-character.rationale: Orwell stressed English hatred of militarism, so glorifying war is unlikely.

separate-church-state.rationale: Blue Labour values faith in public life and Catholic social teaching, which cuts against strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Blue Labour draws on Christian social teaching for values but not for law as scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: An economically socialist tendency treats justice and defence as core state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: BSW criticises NATO and military build-up while patriotic left-conservatives value a strong defence; no source settles it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Blue Labour speaks of a national community of shared tradition and 'pluralist future' without defining the nation ethnically.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Left-conservatism emphasises materialism, collectivism and class struggle as the Old Left did.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Orwell wanted rough equality of incomes, but Glasman said fairness should reward desert and criticised equality-of-outcome politics.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Left-conservatives reject identity-based New Left causes, but no source addresses indigenous authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism could support it, but rejection of social-justice campaigning argues against; no source addresses it.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some see class struggle as civilizational conflict, but Western left-conservatives stress national rather than civilisational unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Blue Labour stresses reciprocity, mutuality and solidarity against market self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Blue Labour rejects abstract universal values in favour of communal bonds and mutual obligation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose environmentalism but sources say nothing about nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-family and anti-environmentalist stance makes population control unlikely to be backed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Blue Labour and BSW want reindustrialisation and industrial work, not a rejection of industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Blue Labour's conservatism and defence of community and work make disruptive acceleration unwelcome.

human-enhancement.rationale: Social conservatism and defence of traditional values suggest scepticism of body modification.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rejection of technocratic, managerial government and distrust of elites points against delegating decisions to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Sources do not address it and adherents' libertarian-versus-order instincts pull in both directions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Blue Labour looks to pre-war Labour's communities for renewal but wants a new politics, so it neither restores nor discards the past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Orwell and Blue Labour are pragmatic but have programmes of their own, and sources do not state a view.

direct-action.rationale: Blue Labour works through community organising, institutions and parties rather than avoiding parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: Orwell values democratic means for a democratic socialism, but this principle is not stated for the tendency.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Blue Labour and BSW want industrial work and reindustrialisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Blue Labour values work and vocational training in existing trades, not abolishing specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Glasman says fairness should reward desert and contribution, not need alone.

production-for-use.rationale: Marxian economics implies this principle, but Western adherents stress jobs and national industry more than the formula.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Left-conservatives are Marxian and anti-capitalist and emphasise class struggle, though wording on exploitation varies.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Orwell rejected Soviet-style rule and demanded political democracy; Western strands do not seek class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Orwell wanted land nationalised, but collective farming is not discussed and rural family holdings are valued.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialist, anti-American left-conservatives often see wars as products of capitalist powers, but the sources do not spell this out.

taxation-theft.rationale: BSW and the left-conservative economic programme rely on redistribution through high taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Social conservatives accept restricting adult conduct beyond harm, as with drugs and sex work.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Blue Labour places community bonds and reciprocal duties above abstract individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Patriotic duty fits conscription, but anti-militarist and BSW critiques of NATO point away; no source decides.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Blue Labour's community focus and democratic voice are the opposite of exit as a check.

state-as-business.rationale: A socialist tendency wanting public ownership rejects running government like a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Pro-redistribution economics fits the view that freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Opposition to the New Left and liberal lifestyle politics suggests this critique, but no source states it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mainstream left-conservatives do not make racial claims; Blue Labour grounds nation in tradition and community.

organic-representation.rationale: Blue Labour's corporatist, community-rooted politics fits representation through families, communities and trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: Orwell's English socialism rejected totalitarian control of culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Blue Labour speaks of national renewal against a hollowed-out liberal politics.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Orwell hated militarism and BSW is anti-interventionist, so expansion is not supported.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Orwell attacked hereditary privilege and called for democracy.

bound-labor.rationale: A socialist tendency committed to workers' rights rejects bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Left-conservatives reject postmodern New Left theory, but the epistemological claim is not stated.

universal-morality.rationale: Blue Labour rejects abstract universal values in favour of particular ties, while its Catholic strand accepts natural law; no source resolves it.

single-common-good.rationale: Glasman describes a common good built through community reciprocity rather than interest balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: BSW criticises Israel's Gaza war, but no source covers Jewish statehood itself.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Patriotic nationalism could support it, but no source states a position.

revive-national-language.rationale: National culture matters to them but language revival is not discussed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Glasman's German model includes works councils and shared decisions between workers and management.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-style school choice sits badly with left economics, though social conservatives like parental choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Marxian and Keynesian economics supports deficit stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: Left-conservatives are anti-capitalist and reject the claim that political freedom depends on economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Blue Labour talks of virtue ethics, but no source states reliance on rulers' example over law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Blue Labour and BSW back national and popular sovereignty against supranational bodies.

force-without-un.rationale: BSW opposes arms deliveries and military adventures and criticises NATO.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Blue Labour values faith as part of community life and Catholic thought.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: BSW argues a strong welfare state needs social solidarity and so limits immigration; Blue Labour says newcomers should not automatically get equal status.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Blue Labour makes work central and Glasman ties fairness to having worked and paid in.

class-collaboration.rationale: Blue Labour favours corporatist, German-style partnership between labour and management.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Blue Labour exalts inherited national and communal tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Left-conservatives are anti-Western and anti-American but sources do not describe common fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Left-conservatism is tied to left-wing nationalism and patriotism, against international class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Left-conservatives defend traditional family values and oppose bourgeois feminism.

ban-interest.rationale: Glasman criticises finance but regional banks and credit remain part of his model.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: English socialism, equality before the law and patriotism of the common people exclude legal racial separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxian roots imply it, but the tendency uses the state for its aims, so it is a weak fit.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: BSW tolerates traditional fuels for a time and attacks green rules.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Blue Labour stresses shared national culture and rebuilding solidarity, so expecting assimilation fits.

elite-replacement.rationale: Blue Labour and BSW blame elite policy for wages and solidarity, but mainstream adherents do not endorse the replacement conspiracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Sources give no position on electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: Orwell's patriotism is insular and anti-imperial, and BSW opposes interventionism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose intersectionality and New Left feminism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: BSW and left-wing populism attack out-of-touch political elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Defence of family and community dignity rules out eugenic discouragement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Sources do not discuss it and patriotic order concerns compete with accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: An economically socialist tendency is the opposite of minimal-state liberalism.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: English socialism's democratic, anti-hierarchical outlook excludes racial discouragement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Orwell wanted rough equality and an end to privilege, though Blue Labour distrusts abstract universal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Orwell and Blue Labour build socialism on the nation, at odds with the claim that it needs foreign revolutions.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-imperialism could back it but no source addresses it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Faith is valued but no source states a position on civil law uniformity.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Liberal Western left-conservatives rarely seek to restrict conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Western left-conservatism has no such tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Blue Labour values faith and Catholic social teaching in community life, so religious instruction in schools is acceptable.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states held this, but Western strands do not discuss it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: English democratic socialism places political authority on democratic consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionism and reindustrialisation suggest favouring exports, but this is not stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Orwell's gentleness and legalism, and mainstream democratic practice, rule out forced expulsion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A socialist tendency accepts state coercion for taxes and regulation, rejecting the non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Blue Labour champions reciprocity and solidarity and criticises market competition's effect on work and community.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Orwell defended legality and liberties; sources do not address party bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Glasman's guild-republican language of resisting concentrated power fits, but this exact claim is not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: Orwell valued English respect for legality and constitutional government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Orwell opposed Leninism and Blue Labour works through community organising.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left economics and Catholic social teaching in Blue Labour support priority for the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Home ownership fits working-class aspiration, while Blue Labour criticises Thatcherite market politics; adherents differ.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Pro-union tendency opposes restricting strikes, though Glasman criticised public-sector union power.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxian economics attributes poverty to social and economic structures, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: BSW and Blue Labour both argue immigration weakens the solidarity a welfare state needs.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Blue Labour's community politics relies on representation and institutions, not sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Orwell valued respect for legality, though order concerns could ease this.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Marxian and Keynesian economics accepts state price intervention in scarcity.

party-controls-media.rationale: Orwell opposed totalitarian control of information; Western strands support democratic pluralism.

party-commands-army.rationale: Orwell's democratic English socialism does not subordinate the army to a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Glasman said newcomers should not automatically have equal status as those already here.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Old Left egalitarianism would favour it, but sources give no position.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Old Left parties value discipline, but BSW and Blue Labour do not state this.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Blue Labour backs Lexit and BSW opposes European federalism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Orwell wanted parliamentary democracy and a republic-like reordering of the officer corps.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed by sources; Blue Labour includes Catholic and Anglican strands.

clerical-rule.rationale: Orwell's English socialism is a lay democratic project, and Blue Labour wants faith as a community force, not clerical government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Orwell argued that patriotism and socialism were no longer opposed and backed the national war effort, so working for one's own side's defeat runs against the patriotic left; no source treats the exact doctrine.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Social conservatism leans toward moral limits on art while the Orwellian free-speech inheritance leans against them, and the sources take no position.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Sources say nothing on presidential term limits, and nothing in the economic or cultural core points either way.

recall-officials.rationale: Left-populist hostility to out-of-touch elites fits letting voters remove officials, though no source states the mechanism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: BSW criticises NATO and wants détente with Russia, which leans toward fewer permanent alliances, but it stops short of a stated demand to end them.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Nothing in left-conservative economics or Blue Labour's community model favours banning rented housing; socialist housing policy normally expands public and regulated renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Orwell's 1941 wartime essay wanted a democratised, class-free army rather than abolishing the professional force, and later sources say nothing on militias.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Blue Labour prizes community and tradition but does not claim country life is morally better than city life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Strong national sentiment suggests sympathy for reunification, but no source states a position on divided nations.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Orwell condemned the left intelligentsia as cut off from the English common people and Glasman attacks 'bossy progressivism' and managerial Fabianism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Blue Labour rejects abstract universal values and stresses attachment to one's own national tradition, but it does not rank civilizations explicitly.

death-penalty.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to abolishing capital punishment among the tendency's social positions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose the New Left's gender politics and BSW opposes gender-ideology measures, which points against sex and gender-equality curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Faith matters to Blue Labour but Marxian materialism and working-class respect for science mean teaching creationism is not a stated aim.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatism and opposition to sex work suggest support for restricting pornography, but sources do not mention it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Blue Labour wants newcomers not to have automatic equal status but nothing indicates whether citizenship follows blood or birthplace.

minority-language-support.rationale: No source covers minority-language policy and the tendency's national and class priorities do not point either way.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Faith is respected as part of community life, but no source discusses exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Communal conformity and attachment to custom outweigh Millian experiments in living, though Orwell prized English 'privateness'.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialism and anti-capitalist economics lean toward debt relief for poor countries, but sources do not state it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxian anti-imperialist logic holds that formal independence without economic transformation is hollow, but no source applies it here.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Sources do not address constitutional rewriting and the tendency's democratic instincts do not decide it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Western strands insist on democracy as Orwell did, while Chinese left-conservatives differ, so a typical Western adherent rejects it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Socialist universalism favours aid but nation-first and anti-globalist priorities weigh against it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Patriotic sovereigntism supports national deterrence while BSW criticises military build-up; sources do not resolve it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Left-populism might favour direct election, but sources give no position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Marxian and Keynesian economics prefer elected governments steering money and the economy over an independent price-stability mandate.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: BSW backs a Gaza ceasefire but no source states a general rule on exchanging land for peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Blue Labour's reciprocity and Orwell's common ownership of land and industry both subordinate property rights to the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Old Left Marxist-Leninist strands treat the USSR as a socialist state, and Orwell criticised its totalitarianism without calling it state capitalism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: BSW is sceptical of costly green regulation, which suggests reluctance to act ahead of scientific proof, though sources do not mention the principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Patriotic left-conservatives value national defence but BSW criticises NATO, and sources do not resolve the allied-attack rule.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: BSW opposes sanctions and arms for Ukraine, but no source addresses annexation law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Blue Labour values faith in communal life and draws on Catholic social teaching, so it would not curb religious institutions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Orwell expected the royal family could remain as a national symbol after the revolution, which fits a non-partisan head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity matters to Blue Labour but sources do not address secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No source treats regional autonomy within a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Orwell's democratic socialism sets itself against hereditary privilege and sacral monarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: BSW wants higher taxes on the wealthy and redistribution, which a flat rate would contradict.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxian materialism favours social causes of character, though left-conservatives also stress tradition and nature in the family.

space-expansion.rationale: Blue Labour's priorities are community, work and local renewal, and sources never mention space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Blue Labour praises pre-war Labour's constitutional conservatism but sources do not describe a mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Orwell's anti-totalitarian English socialism opposes mass leader worship.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family conservatism and concern for fathers pull one way while traditional roles pull another, and sources are silent.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This Maoist thesis belongs to the Marxist-Leninist family and is not part of Western left-conservative thinking.

land-redistribution.rationale: Orwell's programme nationalises land, which implies breaking up great estates, but no source states redistribution to farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: BSW criticises Israel's Gaza war but no source states a right of return for refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Blue Labour's nationalism is civic and patriotic rather than irredentist, though sources do not rule it out.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Orwell's liberal-democratic English socialism and Blue Labour's pluralism have no place for legal punishment of leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: English-liberty socialism and Blue Labour reject legally compelled dress.

common-currency.rationale: Blue Labour backs Lexit and BSW opposes European federalism, which makes a shared currency undesirable.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Their nationalism is national and civic, not a pan-ethnic project.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: No source addresses minority cultural self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources do not address diaspora politics or emigration versus staying.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Left-conservatism emphasises Marxian materialism and class struggle, in line with the Old Left.

ban-cartels.rationale: BSW calls for state intervention against dominant companies and concentrated economic power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Left economics usually saves jobs through public money while BSW attacks big business and banks; sources give no bailout stance.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populism favours majority will while Orwell prized English respect for legality; sources do not settle it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The British parliamentary tradition Orwell and Glasman defend has no entrenched bill of rights, and sources do not discuss one.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-imperialism could support it but no source addresses colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: Orwell wanted political democracy and an end to hereditary privilege, though he accepted a symbolic crown.

minority-veto.rationale: A communal, majoritarian politics of the common good rejects giving any single member a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Orwell's tradition values legality but no source discusses resisting rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Orwell and Glasman both treat the parliamentary constitution as the framework of English socialism, with the monarch symbolic.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Orwell notes the English love of animals but sources give no position on animal ethics.

animal-use-humane.rationale: English-character humane treatment of animals fits keeping and using them with minimal suffering, though sources do not address farming or research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Blue Labour stresses reciprocity and duties of the privileged to the community, though it rejects condescending Fabian paternalism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Blue Labour is a project of organised community politics and reciprocity, opposed to withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxian roots suggest sympathy but social conservatives see mass culture as decay rather than pacification, and sources are silent.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Gramscian idea is not stated in the sources for this tendency.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Left-conservatives are anti-imperialist and anti-capitalist, which fits a core-periphery critique, though no source states it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Blue Labour wants newcomers not to have automatic equal status but sources do not mention office-holding.

party-own-road.rationale: Left-wing nationalism implies each party finding a national road without foreign direction, but sources do not say so.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Sources do not address development strategy for poor countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No source states positions on lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Left-conservatives reject identity-based New Left politics, which points against the claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Old Left and Orwell's wartime politics were anti-fascist, though sources do not discuss constitutional design.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Orwell condemned both Nazism and Stalinism as totalitarian, but Old Left strands reject equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Left tradition with its Marxian materialism treats slavery as the central cause of the war, and nothing in left-conservatism contradicts that.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Blue Labour seeks to reclaim patriotism and national memory against anti-patriotism.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose New Left and bourgeois feminism and defend working-class men's concerns.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Sources do not address domestic violence policy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Anti-Western Chinese strands would agree but Western left-conservatives rarely argue it, and sources are silent.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Orwell wanted a democratised army under civilian control rather than a political guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Family-centred conservatism and left economics diverge, and sources do not address the question.

filial-duty.rationale: Family and mutual obligation are central to Blue Labour's politics.

office-by-exam.rationale: Sources do not address civil service recruitment.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Defence of the family suggests reluctance, though no source addresses divorce law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Sources do not address the delegate model of representation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Left economics favours state pay-as-you-go pensions and opposes privatised accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Orwell nationalises land but keeps a home of one's own, so use-based tenure for individuals is not the model.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Orwell's democratic socialism and Glasman's constitutional conservatism accept parliamentary control of the purse.

single-official-language.rationale: Stress on common national culture suggests a shared language, but sources do not state it.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism and protectionism favour national control of land and assets.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Left-conservatives reject social-justice campaigns not tied to class and oppose intersectionality.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Blue Labour holds that market society corrodes work, community and meaning.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: BSW opposes arms deliveries and military interference abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-imperialist and anti-hegemonic outlook opposes great-power interference in allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: BSW and left populism attack corporate power and lobbying as central grievances.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sovereigntism supports it but sources do not mention NGO funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family-centred and anti-immigration positions favour supporting domestic families rather than immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Localism favours it but sources do not mention it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Keynesian and Marxian economics supports full employment and work as a source of dignity.

democratic-peace.rationale: BSW rejects exporting democracy by force and NATO-led policy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Orwell stressed English respect for legality and Blue Labour stresses duty and reciprocity.

non-intervention.rationale: BSW opposes arms deliveries, sanctions and foreign interventions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream adherents blame elite economic choices, not an ethnic or religious minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The family is a central pillar of Blue Labour and left-conservatism.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Anti-elite populism fits transparency, but sources do not state it.

local-production.rationale: Reindustrialisation and protection of domestic industry favour producing near where goods are consumed.

informal-organisation.rationale: Blue Labour builds institutions and parties, not leaderless affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereigntist Lexit and Eurosceptic politics gives national law priority.

religious-nation.rationale: Blue Labour values faith but defines the nation by shared life and patriotism, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Left-conservatives are anti-American and anti-hegemonic and reject tributary deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Redistribution and solidarity favour sharing revenue across regions, though Blue Labour values localism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Orwell says socialism means common ownership of the means of production while clothes and furniture stay private.

defeat-communism.rationale: Left-conservatives draw on Marxist-Leninist traditions and are anti-Western, so they reject a drive to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: BSW and Blue Labour prefer public provision and local democratic control to a market of mixed providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Blue Labour holds faith to be part of community life and draws on Catholic social teaching.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anti-capitalist Marxian thought concedes capitalism's historical dynamism, but left-conservatives stress its harm to work and community.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxian economics would say yes, but left-conservatives reject bourgeois feminism; sources are silent.

socialized-care.rationale: Family is central, so housework and childcare stay with families.

treaties-binding.rationale: Sources do not address treaties with nations within borders.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Blue Labour's community focus is not a call for property-holding communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not part of Western left-conservatism, which focuses on welfare and solidarity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way phrasing appears in Blue Labour's conservatism and Polanyi-style critique while Marxist-Leninist strands reject it.

historical-land-claim.rationale: BSW criticises Israel's war in Gaza but sources do not discuss historic land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Orwell's anti-fascist socialism and mainstream adherents reject Holocaust denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The tendency opposes LGBT rights but Western strands do not seek criminal penalties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Democratic English socialism rejects suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Faith valued but Blue Labour is pluralist and does not seek blasphemy law.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A doctrine of Islamic jihad is not part of left-conservatism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Democratic socialism rejects removing rulers by force for lacking religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Blue Labour's community organising fits participation in communities and workplaces.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Left-conservatives reject intersectionality and put class first.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: BSW opposes looser rules on changing legal gender and left-conservatives are linked to gender-critical views.

assisted-dying.rationale: Faith and family-centred conservatism suggest opposition, though sources do not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The tendency itself combines left and right but remains within the left on economics, and sources do not say it considers the division obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Blue Labour says profit-maximising capitalism undermines work-based identity and meaning.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Sources do not address Islam; adherents in Europe differ.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Democratic consent underlies English socialism, though faith informs Blue Labour.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Sources do not address religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Sources do not address the issue.

social-market-economy.rationale: Glasman admires the German model, but left-conservatives go further than a social market with public ownership.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Orwell wanted a reformed army, not abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Anti-capitalist redistribution opposes letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: BSW opposes NATO and calls for détente and negotiations.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Orwell accepted a symbolic crown but opposed hereditary privilege in power.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Regional banks appear in Glasman's German model but sources do not describe cost-price mutual credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Keynesian anti-austerity economics supports resisting lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Orwell's programme demands political democracy and an end to privilege.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose environmentalism and New Left feminism.

reification.rationale: Marxist but the sources do not state the doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxian critique of class power fits it, though not stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Western strands do not seek to restrict interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream adherents reject boycotts of minorities.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anti-capitalist class analysis and Orwell's attack on inherited privilege treat concentrated wealth as a threat.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Orwell singled out English respect for legality as a national trait that socialism must build on, so a ruler above the law is rejected.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose the New Left's identity politics and BSW criticises left-liberal lifestyle politics, which includes mandatory gender quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: BSW and Blue Labour favour protecting domestic industry and deglobalisation, but a closed imperial bloc is not an aim and Orwell opposed colonial exploitation.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Blue Labour wants to rebuild trade on worker-protective terms against global capital, so binding labour standards fit, though environmental clauses sit less easily with BSW's green scepticism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states experimented with moral incentives, but Western strands, which stress wages and collective bargaining, do not state a view.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Orwell's English socialism wanted a democratic, popular revolution, and Western left-conservatives do not endorse foco insurgency.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Orwell demanded an end to hereditary privilege, especially in education and inherited incomes, though he accepted a symbolic crown.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Blue Labour's national renewal and rejection of anti-patriotism favour school history centred on one's own nation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Orwell criticised imperial rule and wanted England freed from the decadent imperial ruling class.

patriotic-education.rationale: Blue Labour seeks to reclaim patriotism for the left and Orwell blamed the left intelligentsia for deriding English institutions.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Left-conservatives reject social-justice campaigns not tied to class and opposes New Left identity politics, favouring class-based rather than racial remedies.

public-money-creation.rationale: Orwell would nationalise banks and Keynesian and Marxian economics favours public control of money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxian materialism expects capitalism's crises to recur, though left-conservatives rarely theorise collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Left-conservatives are anti-imperialist and anti-Western, which counts against cultivating influence in former colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: BSW favours deglobalisation and protecting domestic industry, but the question concerns poor countries and sources do not apply it to them.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Left-conservatives are anti-imperialist but also defend workers in their own countries as exploited, so they would not accept the statement fully; sources are silent.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Left economics and opposition to unrestrained markets reject unlimited private freedom to refuse service or work, even though social conservatives dislike anti-discrimination law.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blue Labour backs protectionism and economic sovereignty and BSW wants domestic industry shielded from foreign control.

industrial-unions.rationale: Glasman's German model of industry-wide works councils and bargaining suggests industry-based organisation, though sources do not mention craft versus industrial unions.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Opposition to LGBT rights is a defining social position, though sources do not mention military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Blue Labour treats faith as part of working-class community life, so state atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Left-conservatives are order-minded and retain capital punishment, so abolishing police and prisons is far from their view.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Sources do not discuss consociational government and the tendency's nation-state emphasis does not decide it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: BSW wants a strong welfare state and Blue Labour backs public services run locally, not replacing them with charity.

term-limits.rationale: Sources do not address term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Sources do not address liquid democracy.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Blue Labour's priorities are community, work and nation, and the sources suggest no emphasis on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Blue Labour draws on Catholic and Anglican traditions with different views and the sources do not say.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Defence of traditional family roles pulls toward male headship while egalitarian socialist heritage pulls the other way, and no source says.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Glasman says newcomers should not automatically have the same status as those already here.

rent-control.rationale: Pro-redistribution Marxian and Keynesian economics favours legal limits on rents.

abolish-ip.rationale: Sources say nothing on patents and copyright, and the tendency's industrial protectionism points to keeping them.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Patriotic education fits, but Western left-conservatives do not advocate drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: BSW criticises NATO and military build-up, which suggests opposing foreign nuclear weapons on home soil.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: BSW is critical of NATO and anti-American, and sovereigntism opposes foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Sources do not address recognition of genocides.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Glasman says fairness should reward desert, work and contribution, and Orwell wanted inherited incomes ended.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Orwell, a patriotic wartime socialist, rejected pacifism and defended armed national defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Blue Labour's emphasis on inherited national tradition fits it, but sources do not state a thesis of ancient continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Left-conservatives are associated with gender-critical feminism, which holds that sex is biological.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Gender-critical feminism, tied to left-conservatism, rests on a fixed category of women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Patriotism favours honouring the nation's war dead, but sacralising martyrs is not stated.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Blue Labour draws on Christian ethics but treats politics as reciprocity and negotiation, not cosmic struggle.

culture-before-state.rationale: Blue Labour puts civil society before the state but sources do not address nation-building.

god-not-male.rationale: Sources do not address theology of gender.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose feminist critique of traditional values.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Blue Labour's patriotism is civic and class-based, not about majority control of commerce.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Sources do not address regional mergers.

independent-unions.rationale: Glasman defends unions as autonomous bodies of reciprocity, and Blue Labour wants pro-worker movements, not state-run unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Orwell and Old Left Marxism hold that socialism requires working-class power, though Western left-conservatives define it through national community.

local-essentials-public.rationale: BSW proposes public ownership of key industries and Blue Labour wants local services under democratic management.

second-chamber.rationale: Orwell wanted the House of Lords abolished as hereditary privilege, but later sources do not say.

municipal-property.rationale: Blue Labour favours local control but sources do not call for municipally owned means of production, and Orwell wanted national ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Blue Labour favours localism within a nation-state with national parliament, not confederations of towns.

family-wage.rationale: Family is central to Blue Labour and work is meant to support family life.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Sources do not address regulation of medicines.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Sources do not address ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State-centred tendency and order-minded politics favour traceable payments, though no source states it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Sources do not address online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Blue Labour's Catholic strands favour personalism but its communal emphasis treats persons through their ties; sources are mixed.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Blue Labour holds that faith matters in human life and draws on Catholic social teaching.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Blue Labour wants local democratic management but sources do not address constitutional basis of autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Sources do not address agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: Blue Labour's attachment to local communities and BSW's scepticism of green policy do not favour urban densification.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The tendency sees class, not race, as the basis of political interest and opposes identity politics.

racial-pride.rationale: Left-conservatives reject identity politics but defend national pride, and sources do not say.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: BSW opposes foreign interventions and Orwell stressed English hatred of militarism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Sources do not define nationhood by language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Orwell's democratic socialism and Blue Labour's common national community reject separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sources do not address foreign partition plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Pro-redistribution economics supports tuition-free public universities, though Blue Labour prefers vocational training.

pollution-taxes.rationale: BSW is sceptical of green taxation and favours public intervention; sources do not say.

future-generations.rationale: Sources do not address it and their green scepticism pulls against it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Social conservatives and gender-critical feminists hold that women differ, but sources do not state the claim about public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: BSW criticises military build-up but patriotic defence matters; no source states it.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anti-elite populism and Orwell's democratic socialism lean toward open diplomacy, though sources do not state it.

capital-controls.rationale: Blue Labour wants national economic sovereignty against global finance and BSW wants deglobalisation.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: An order-minded state-centred politics favours it, but no source states it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Orwell backed national defence and patriotic soldiering.

collective-bargaining.rationale: BSW calls for strengthening collective bargaining and Glasman's German model rests on it.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Glasman rejects state top-ups as a substitute for wages and work-based fairness, but sources do not address credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Marxian and Keynesian economics rejects binding limits on public borrowing.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: BSW's anti-globalism and anti-Western economic orientation favour restructuring international economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Orwell wanted democratic socialism through the existing English constitution, not smashing the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The tendency has a definite blueprint of public ownership and protection and does not accept no fixed blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose environmentalism and market-style valuation of nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Blue Labour's national renewal and patriotism give the nation moral weight, though the term sacred overstates it.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Pro-redistribution economics supports relief, but sources do not state it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Sources do not address regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Blue Labour's Aristotelian virtue ethics and Catholic social teaching presuppose a shared human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Public ownership and anti-elite media critique both fit, but sources do not state it.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Sources do not address religious pluralism in this sense.

farm-price-support.rationale: BSW and Blue Labour favour state protection of domestic producers from market forces.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: BSW criticises military build-up and patriots defend national security, so sources do not decide this.

workers-own-party.rationale: Blue Labour aims to win back working people to Labour and Old Left traditions favour a workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Left-conservatives defend protecting the vulnerable and oppose it, though sources do not mention FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Left egalitarianism supports equal property rights, though sources do not mention it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Sources do not address linguistic disputes.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The tendency prefers public regulation to tort law, but sources do not say.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The South African MK party supports traditional leaders, but Western strands do not, so a typical adherent does not.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: BSW opposes costly green rules and left-conservatives oppose environmentalism.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Order-minded social conservatism leans toward fixed sentences, though sources are silent.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Blue Labour stresses shared national culture and solidarity, which includes a common language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Pro-union, collective-bargaining politics supports union security.

voter-id.rationale: Sources do not address voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Sources do not address legal status of religious interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Orwell stressed economic equality as well as democracy, and sources do not define it procedurally.

premarital-sex.rationale: Family-centred social conservatism leans toward disapproval but sources do not state it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Democratic English socialism and legalism oppose arbitrary shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Blue Labour makes work and desert central and wants community-run services, not replacing welfare with cash payments.

women-suffrage.rationale: Orwell's programme demands political democracy and equality, and nothing in left-conservatism opposes women's suffrage.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Blue Labour treats faith as part of community life and left-conservatives defend traditional family values.

race-social-construct.rationale: Left-conservatives reject identity-based scholarship but also reject racial determinism, and sources do not state it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Left-conservatives oppose bourgeois feminism and state feminism.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Orwell's common ownership of land and the tendency's socialist economics reject first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: BSW prioritises sovereignty but criticises great-power wars, and sources do not say.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Blue Labour values faith but its Catholic and Anglican strands do not stress literal inerrancy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands would agree but Western left-conservatives do not discuss it.

indirect-election.rationale: Orwell wanted direct democracy through parliament and sources do not discuss councils.

national-church-status.rationale: Blue Labour's conservatism toward the constitution and valuing faith lean toward the established church, though Glasman criticises Anglican supremacism.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: National unity emphasis leans against ethnic autonomy, but sources do not say.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Democratic socialism favours consent of inhabitants, though sources do not say.

simple-living.rationale: Blue Labour criticises consumerism but also stresses work and prosperity for workers.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Blue Labour's patriotism rooted in England gives homeland moral weight, though not as a spiritual duty.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Orwell stressed legality and democratic socialism rejects killings without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: BSW praises the Chinese economic model and opposes naval deployments toward China.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Orwell's nationalisation of land and mines implies common ownership of natural resources, but compensation to all is not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Blue Labour's communal reciprocity and Marxian economics reject strong self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Left economics dislikes regressive sales taxes, but sources do not address them.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: BSW wants a strong welfare state built on solidarity, which favours universal over narrowly targeted programmes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Blue Labour works through parties and organised community groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: BSW opposes dominant companies and corporate influence, which fits ending special privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Blue Labour's Catholic social teaching strand and faith politics pull against, but sources do not say.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Blue Labour pairs modern economic reindustrialisation with traditional family, faith and nation.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Orwell's democratic equality implies equal legal standing, though family conservatism pulls the other way; sources do not say.

national-resource-control.rationale: BSW favours state control of key industries and national sovereignty over strategic assets.

material-over-identity.rationale: BSW criticises left-liberal lifestyle politics for neglecting workers, and left-conservatism rejects social-justice campaigns not tied to class struggle.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Orwell held socialism and patriotism complementary and Blue Labour seeks to reclaim patriotism for the left.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The ideology keeps redistribution and public ownership, so it judges a distribution by its outcome as well as by how it arose.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from hostility to global finance and support for domestic industry, which favours curbs on speculation; not stated in the sources.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Left-conservatives are sceptical of identity politics yet differ on racism's weight; adherents are split, so inferred neutral.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The ideology says little on natural law; adherents split between respecting settled law and tradition and resisting unjust rules.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Blue Labour stresses the dignity of work and jobs for communities, so mass automation to end work is inferred to be unwelcome.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Euroscepticism and scepticism of military alliances, which favour independent national centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Its Marxian-influenced economics and focus on working people point towards labour as the source of value; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The audit excludes one-party Marxist-Leninist variants; its adherents favour democratic politics, so a communist-party-led market is inferred to be rejected.

missingStatements.text: The political left should concentrate on workers' material interests rather than cultural identity issues.
missingStatements.rationale: BSW criticises left-liberal lifestyle politics for neglecting workers, and left-conservatism rejects social-justice campaigns not tied to class struggle.

missingStatements.text: Large-scale immigration lowers wages and weakens the solidarity that sustains a welfare state.
missingStatements.rationale: Glasman called immigration an unofficial wages policy and BSW argues a strong welfare state needs social solidarity.

missingStatements.text: Patriotism is compatible with, and necessary to, a left politics that serves ordinary people.
missingStatements.rationale: Orwell held socialism and patriotism complementary and Blue Labour seeks to reclaim patriotism for the left.

notes: Marxist-Leninist and ruling-party variants (China, Cambodia, Tanzania, South Africa) would answer differently on one-party rule, monarchy and religion. Many answers on culture-war and foreign-policy detail are low-confidence extrapolations from the core combination.
